author: U. N. Kim
title: Maui County opens Makahiki Grant Program application period for 2027 funding
text:
The County Office of the Mayor, through its Office of Economic Development, announced on June 10 that the Fiscal Year 2027 Makahiki Grant Program application period is open through 5 p.m. July 10, 2026. The program is offered in partnership with the County of Maui Department of ʻŌiwi Resources. Applications and full program details are available online.
A total of $850,000 in grant funding will be distributed to organizations, community groups, educational institutions, cultural practitioners, businesses and other eligible applicants who wish to develop programs and activities recognizing the Makahiki season throughout Maui County.
“Through this initiative, we hope to support and empower community-led efforts that celebrate the values and traditions of Makahiki while creating meaningful opportunities for residents and visitors alike to learn, participate and connect,” Mayor Richard Bissen said. “Makahiki reminds us of the importance of gratitude, stewardship, peace and community. This program is an opportunity to bring those values to life across our County.”
Traditionally observed during Hoʻoilo (the winter months), Makahiki season begins with the first rising of Makaliʻi (Pleiades) at sunset and lasts four months honoring Lono—the god associated with agriculture and fertility.
The new grant program aims to celebrate Hawaiian culture while promoting stewardship, well-being, local economic opportunity and advancing the theme: “Rest. Grow. Sustain.” Eligible proposals may include cultural festivals; educational workshops; agricultural activities; traditional games; art programs; community volunteer initiatives; small business events; youth programming; wellness activities; innovative projects supporting participation in Makahiki season; or activities fostering prosperity, unity or renewal within communities.
According to officials from OED, collaboration among organizations is encouraged as part of a broader commitment by Maui County toward strengthening its kamaʻāina economy by supporting local businesses as well as cultural practitioners, while creating opportunities for residents to connect through shared experiences.
